extracted.intended_audience: joint force public affairs officers (PAOs), MOC directors, commanders, and PA staff supporting military joint operations
extracted.subtask_description: Doctrine and operational guidance for conducting public affairs (media relations, media operations centers, assessment, command information, and related functions) in joint military operations, including domestic support and multinational environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous dialogue with media / media access
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need for continuous dialogue between the joint force and the media who are covering its activities; open and independent reporting are the principal means of coverage of military operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders should seek regular opportunities to work with the media. Media coverage can shape public perception; JFCs and PAOs should continually assess effects of actions and signals on perceptions, attitudes, and beliefs, and should formulate and deliver timely and culturally attuned messages for US publics, allied/partner publics, and publics in countries where the US conducts operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA personnel act as liaisons but do not interfere with reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: PA personnel should act as liaisons but should not interfere with the reporting process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PA mission includes helping media representatives understand joint force events and occurrences so that media coverage is accurate. The JFC or a designated representative should conduct frequent operational briefings to inform audiences and respond to media questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational briefings frequency and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The JFC, or a designated representative, should conduct frequent operational briefings to inform internal and external audiences of current military operations and respond to media questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefings help ensure accurate coverage and provide opportunities to formulate timely, culturally attuned messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for credentialing journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for credentialing journalists are established by the joint force PAO or the MOC director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credentialing is not intended to be a control measure or means to restrict certain media outlets; it primarily validates individuals as journalists, enhances their ability to report, and ensures that if captured they are recognized as journalists under the law of war. Embedded reporters will be registered and carry identifying credentials or Geneva Convention cards as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC role in credentialing and ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The MOC serves as a logistic and information base for media relations operations and sets credentialing criteria and ground rules tailored to specific joint operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists seeking credentials from the MOC are asked to agree to ground rules tailored to the specific, ongoing joint operation. Commanders should not provide information to non-credentialed, unregistered journalists without guidance from the joint force PAO or the MOC director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration encouragement for non-credentialed journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: All journalists should be considered for media pools and strongly encouraged to register with the MOC, even if not credentialed by DOD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request that non-credentialed journalists abide by the same established media ground rules during registration. Absence of DOD credential does not preclude inclusion in media pools, but access may be different.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension or expulsion of media credential
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to suspend credentials or expel a reporter should only be made with the concurrence of the JFC and the CCDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend/expel only under circumstances warranting such action and after appropriate command concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media ground rules purpose and elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground rules are developed to protect members of DOD from the release of information that could threaten their security or safety during ongoing operations yet facilitate the media’s access to timely, relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground rules reconcile media desire to cover operations with DOD security and safety concerns and are not intended to prevent release of derogatory or negative information. They should include the process for release of information, media access to the commander, access to the Internet if not commercially available, and the process for unintentional exposure to classified information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multinational operations: ground rules and credentialing responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: In multinational operations, responsibilities for establishing media ground rules, credentialing media, and expulsion are developed and implemented through appropriate multinational command and staff channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media outlets owned wholly/partly by rival states might not receive same considerations as those from friendly nations. Non-credentialed journalists should be encouraged to register at the appropriate information center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escorts: identification, training, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Often the media will not be accompanied by PA personnel; commanders, with PA assistance, should identify shortages of escorts and provide training for non-PA personnel who will serve as escorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escorts need not be PA personnel but should be knowledgeable members who received media relations training. They should facilitate reporters, not interfere with reporting or attempt to inhibit military personnel from talking about their jobs consistent with security and operational restrictions. Commanders must develop unit plans tailored to local conditions to accommodate reporters and issue guidance about information/support provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media pools are exceptional and temporary
rubrics_metrics.description: Pools are not to serve as the standard means of covering US military operations; they may sometimes provide the only feasible means of early access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pools should be as large as possible and be disbanded at the earliest opportunity—within 24 to 36 hours when possible. The arrival of early-access pools does not cancel the principle of independent coverage for journalists already in the area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media pool composition and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain conditions (remote locations, ships, limited space), PA plans should specify the number and types of media (including internal media) who will form the pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The military determines the size and composition of the pool, usually establishing categories such as print, broadcast, and trade media to ensure adequate scope and distribution. The media representatives should determine who fills the spaces in the pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military responsibility for transportation of pools
rubrics_metrics.description: The military is responsible for the transportation of pools and should provide dedicated transportation if able.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure complete coverage, commanders should provide transportation; under open coverage, JFCs should authorize field commanders to permit journalists to ride on military vehicles/aircraft when feasible. Commanders should follow The Joint Travel Regulations, Volume 2, to ensure standardization of policy/procedures. PA planning should include reimbursement from media depending on location and availability of commercial transportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and transmission support for media
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders should supply PA personnel with facilities to ensure timely, secure, compatible transmission of pool and independent material; provide access to communications facilities for news products prepared by the pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When government facilities are unavailable, media should file by any other available means. Commanders should understand media communications capabilities and engage in early discussions to deconflict the electromagnetic spectrum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security review and OPSEC coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: PA officers should work closely with OPSEC planners to develop guidelines to prevent inadvertent disclosure of critical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA supports OPSEC through strict adherence to established security review programs and other measures to ensure critical information is protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA staff organization and dedicated functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PA staff should be organized and have staff members dedicated to management, plans (future operations and future plans), media operations/MOC, analysis and assessment, command information/community engagement, Internet, and administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The size and organization of a joint force PA staff varies to accommodate mission requirements; structure should improve PA support to the JFC in the information environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint force PAO responsibility to the JFC
rubrics_metrics.description: The joint force PAO is responsible to the JFC for directing PA activities and provides PA counsel and support to the commander.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joint force PAO, with appropriate staff support, is on the commander's personal staff and is directly responsible for all the JFC’s PA requirements and oversight of PA functions and subordinate MOCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC director responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The MOC director, with supporting MOC staff, is responsible for coordinating all media operations within the operational area and provides and coordinates support to the JFC through the joint force PAO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MOC director coordinates with J-2, J-3, and foreign disclosure officers to ensure releasable information is accurate, timely, and issued within OPSEC guidance, considering HN sensitivities and media guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: participate in operational analysis, planning, execution, and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: PA personnel participate in operational analysis, planning, execution, and assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA integration into operational planning ensures communications strategies align with operational objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: participate in cross-functional staff organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in all applicable cross-functional staff organizations (e.g., boards, centers, cells).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PA representation and integration across staff structures to coordinate messaging and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: develop and coordinate communication strategies and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and coordinate communication strategies and guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert strategic guidance into communicable themes and plans that support mission goals and account for audiences and cultural considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: prepare PA annexes and support other annex development
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare PA annexes and support other annex development, as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA annexes should delineate processes, responsibilities, and coordination mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: execute and assess communication strategies and plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Execute and assess communication strategies and plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should inform adjustments during execution to improve effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: evaluate PA resources and provide assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate PA resources and provide assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure resources align with mission needs; modify resourcing as assessments dictate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: recommend future PA priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Make recommendations on future PA priorities, near and long term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assessments and operational context to inform priorities for messaging, resourcing, and capability development.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: coordinate PA activities with other US agencies, HN, and NGOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate PA activities with other US agencies, host nation (HN), and NGOs as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interagency and multinational coordination is critical to ensure message consistency and leverage partner capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: identify intelligence requirements to support PA planning and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify intelligence requirements to support PA planning and assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with J-2 and intelligence staff to acquire relevant information that informs messaging and assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: identify visual information (VI) and imagery requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify VI and imagery requirements to the J-3 or designated representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate VI tasking that supports PA objectives and ensure imagery availability for PA use consistent with OPSEC/INFOSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: establish and manage a MOC
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and manage a Media Operations Center (MOC) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOC should be resourced, staffed, and located to facilitate media access and coordination with PA staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: monitor/assess public opinion and media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor/assess public opinion, media coverage, and sentiment analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monitoring outputs to inform message adjustments and strategic communications decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: modify communication strategies based on assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify communication strategies and plans based on assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment-driven modification improves alignment with objectives and audience perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: plan, coordinate, and assess community engagement activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan, coordinate, and assess community engagement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with country team and HN to identify engagement opportunities that support mission and relationship-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: develop, execute, and assess command information programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop, execute, and assess command information programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure internal messaging supports morale, situational awareness, and consistency with external communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: provide content for publicly accessible websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide content for publicly accessible websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Web content should convey mission context, be timely, and support broader communications strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: integrate social media into PA activities IAW DOD policy
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with DOD policy, integrate social media into all PA activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social media strategically, ensure PA personnel conduct interactive activities (with journalists or established news organization equivalents), and ensure messages are culturally appropriate and in the language/idiom of the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: provide media training to potential spokespersons
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide media training to potential spokespersons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training prepares commanders and subject matter experts to interact with media effectively and within OPSEC constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: disseminate timely, accurate information about military activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminate timely, accurate information about military activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize accuracy and timeliness; do not withhold derogatory or negative information solely to avoid embarrassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: respond to media and public inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to media and public inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track queries and provide timely, coordinated responses via the MOC/press desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA action: educate JFCs and staffs on role of information and PA
rubrics_metrics.description: Educate JFCs and staffs on the role of information and PA in operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure commanders understand the impact of information and the requirement to integrate PA early into planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative section responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative section provides broad administrative support for the entire PA staff and is responsible for resource support and monitoring status of manning levels and readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section may contract for cultural or linguistic assistance as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans section responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PA planners support future operations and future planning and convert strategic guidance into PA plans for OPORDs and fragmentary orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They participate in applicable boards, bureaus, centers, cells, and working groups to coordinate PA planning throughout the JOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide PA planning and execution support for activities that promote interaction of US forces, multinational partners, and host-nation populations throughout the JOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires close coordination with the country team, HN, CMOC, and IO cell/planners to identify opportunities for the JFC and key staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis and assessment responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: This section supports both plans and media operations/MOC, represents PA in assessment-related cross-functional organizations, and works with J-2 to identify PA assessment requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce assessment products to support current operations and plans sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC as central point of contact and staffing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A MOC is the central point of contact between the military and media representatives covering operations; it should be staffed to support local and regional non-English speaking media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early establishment of MOCs is important to facilitate responsive and efficient media operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: credential media
rubrics_metrics.description: Credential media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOC handles credentialing consistent with command policy and ground rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: maintain a media database
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a media database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Database supports credentialing, tracking, and communications with media representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: coordinate media embeds
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate media embeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage selection, logistics, and ground rules for embedded reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: identify logistic requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify logistic requirements to support media operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for transportation, lodging, messing, equipment, and other necessities for media support.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: obtain/provide vehicles and escorts
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain/provide vehicles (armored as required) and escorts (armed as required) to move media to cover events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure force protection and movement planning support media coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: provide force protection gear to media
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide necessary force protection gear to media representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuance may include helmets, canteens, flak vests, cold weather clothing, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: coordinate subordinate unit PA coverage of critical events
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate subordinate unit PA coverage of critical events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure coherent, deconflicted information products across subordinate units.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: coordinate acquisition and transmission of imagery, information, and interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate the acquisition and transmission of imagery, information, and interviews to support the PA strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate timely collection and distribution of VI to meet media and PA needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: coordinate requirements for VI support including COMCAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate requirements for VI support (including COMCAM) with appropriate staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA should identify imagery requirements that exceed organic capabilities and coordinate tasking with J-3.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: facilitate OPSEC/INFOSEC review of imagery and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitate the review of all imagery and information for OPSEC and INFOSEC issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure releasable material is cleared and does not compromise operations or information security.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: edit and post content to publicly accessible website(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit as necessary and post content to publicly accessible website(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accuracy, timeliness, and consistency with PA strategy and OPSEC guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: produce information packets, news releases, and stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover military operations and produce information packets, news releases, and stories for distribution to external and internal audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide materials to Services’ hometown news centers and PA offices as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: translate releases into major local languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate all releases and disseminate in the major languages indigenous to the people in the operational area and other intended audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use linguistic resources and culturally appropriate messaging to reach target audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: coordinate interview requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate interview requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage scheduling, vetting, and logistical support for media interviews with commanders and subject matter experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: coordinate briefings for local and regional media
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate briefings for local and regional media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate access and ensure culturally and linguistically appropriate engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: coordinate briefings from operational area with US media
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate briefings from the operational area with US media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure US media have timely access to operational perspectives while observing OPSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: receive, respond, and track media queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive, respond, and track media queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of inquiries and responses to ensure accountability and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOC task: support command information activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Support command information activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure external and internal information products are coordinated and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deputy MOC director responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The deputy MOC director assists in management of the MOC and performs director functions when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include oversight of military-media communications, assessment of available published media products, and liaison with joint force operations staff and subordinate commands to ensure continuous flow of timely information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press desk responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel working the press desk interact directly with the media and serve as the primary point of information exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include responding to media inquiries, preparing and issuing news releases, arranging interviews, conducting briefings, preparing joint force operational briefers, assisting senior commanders in media encounters, supervising/integrating media support and HN engagement teams, including reps from non-DOD agencies/NGOs/HN, and possibly sending press desk personnel as liaisons to those organizations. In multinational operations, PA personnel from other countries may work in the press desk to represent their nation’s interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media support section responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The media support section helps the media cover joint force activities and coordinates/manages transportation, communications, logistic support, credentialing, and media pools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section matches media with knowledgeable escorts, ensures security reviews are conducted efficiently, and supports media movement and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing/outreach section responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The marketing/outreach section conducts liaison with media outside the JOA to determine interest in ongoing operations and repurpose or arrange for PA products to support their needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They coordinate remote interviews, produce opinion pieces, speeches, presentations, holiday greetings, special events programming, and coordinate speakers for organizations in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public website responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the Internet provides the JFC a powerful tool to convey information quickly and efficiently on the nature and scope of the JFC’s mission and to counter adversary propaganda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section manages and maintains site content, ensuring it puts operational actions into context and supports public and command information activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive internet activities rules
rubrics_metrics.description: JFCs may allow use of interactive Internet activities (email, blogs, chat rooms, social media) to support operations, IAW current DOD guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise approved, only PA personnel engage in interactive activities with journalists employed by media organizations or with individuals/websites considered equivalent to established news organizations. Activities should be in the language/idiom of the intended audience and use culturally appropriate messages and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring section responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The monitoring section is responsible for monitoring electronic and print media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They develop and distribute summaries and transcripts of media coverage, press conferences, and other significant events to support assessment and messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional media engagement responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: This section establishes and maintains relations between the joint force and local and regional non-English media, facilitates media events, distributes press releases, and monitors/translates their coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff with linguists as required to conduct translations and culturally appropriate engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command information: fair treatment of internal media and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: MOC director should ensure internal media are treated fairly and equally with external media and allotted an appropriate share of limited resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders should provide all external news releases and responses to query to command information channels. AFRTS supplements the PA’s command information mission and generally works as a division within the MOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: COMCAM coordination and imagery access
rubrics_metrics.description: PA should identify and coordinate imagery requirements that exceed organic capabilities with the J-3; COMCAM is a principal provider of VI and generally receives tasking from J-3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All COMCAM imagery should be available to PA for review and possible use consistent with OPSEC and INFOSEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-MOC establishment and function
rubrics_metrics.description: PAO may recommend establishment of sub-MOCs based on operational area size, force dispersion, diversity of Service components, and variety of concurrent missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sub-MOCs are normally smaller than main MOC, perform same functions, may be temporary or established locations, and could be afloat to support maritime aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment purpose and emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment is a process that measures progress of the joint force toward mission accomplishment; the primary emphasis of the PA assessment is identifying, measuring, and evaluating implications within the operational environment that the commander does not control but can influence through a coherent communications strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous assessment helps JFCs and components adjust operations to ensure objectives are met and the military end state is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish baselines and criteria during mission analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment process begins during mission analysis when the commander and staff consider what to measure and how to measure it; baselines for what is going to be measured should be established at this point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PA planners should determine objectives for PA activities that support the JFC’s strategy as well as relevant assessment measures and criteria to determine success. The initial set of criteria becomes the basis for future assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment requires monitoring, measuring, and analyzing multiple sources
rubrics_metrics.description: PA assessments require monitoring, measuring, and analyzing relevant information (media coverage, Internet content, polls, intelligence products, etc.) to evaluate success of PA activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During execution, assessments drive adjustments to current operations and future planning; assessments may identify requirements to revalidate PA resources and modify them accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: understanding of the Iraqi and Pan-Arab media
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding of the Iraqi and Pan-Arab media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a basis for assessing alignment among facts, media framing, and local perceptions (example from Iraq).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: media penetration of key themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Media penetration of key themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure how widely key themes are reaching target media and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: alignment of key messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment of key messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether key messages align across communications and with intended themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: understanding local perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding Iraqi perceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess local population perceptions to determine message resonance and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: prevalence of misinformation and disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevalence of misinformation and disinformation in media stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and quantify misinformation/disinformation to inform counter-messaging and corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment criterion: resonance of press conferences and key themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Resonance of press conferences and key themes and messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure how well press events and themes are influencing media framing and audience perceptions.
